channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Fish Stocks Thrive Thanks to This Pink Seaweed and Locals Who Protected It
item.description: Ten years after islanders won a ban on scallop dredging, the pink seaweed beds and fish stocks are thriving. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Choose hand-dived or creel-caught shellfish over dredged when you buy seafood. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘I pulled him out, I heard more screaming’ – How a Cadet Saved a Father and Son from Drowning
item.description: A merchant marine cadet pulled a father and his son from a swimming pool and both survived. How you can help: Take a short CPR and water rescue course; it is enough to act in an emergency. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved
item.description: Scientists found that hair follicle patterns form by cells following simple chemical signals. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Paralysis Could Not Stop Her: How This 84-year-old Made Good on Her Musical Promise
item.description: An 84-year-old who recovered from paralysis now plays piano for the nursing home that treated her. How you can help: Offer to play music or read aloud at a local care home; many welcome volunteers. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Burnham lauds £12bn offshore wind investment as he prepares for climate summit
item.description: A record 12 billion pound investment will build new offshore wind farms off the Norfolk coast. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: What We’re Reading: An 80-Cent Plastic Bag Is Saving Mothers’ Lives
item.description: A reading roundup led by an 80-cent plastic drape that helps midwives catch dangerous bleeding after birth. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Bid to restore rare Atlantic rainforest secures £6m lottery grant
item.description: A 6 million pound grant will restore rare Atlantic rainforest on Scotland's west coast and train local people. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Join a native woodland planting day; many restoration projects train beginners. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
item.description: Each mosquito species is drawn to its own mix of skin odours, a lead for better-targeted repellents. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
item.description: Fossils from Thailand show a 66-pound rodent lived 34 million years ago, far earlier than expected. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
item.description: A 237-million-year-old armoured amphibian found in China appears to have lived in the sea. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: A young man who lost schooling in lockdown set up peer tutoring for refugee students. How you can help: Offer an hour a week of tutoring through a local refugee support group. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil releases the world’s first fossil fuel phaseout roadmap
item.description: Brazil has published the first national roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
item.description: A new image-cleaning method uncovered a planet hidden in James Webb telescope pictures. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ‘Nothing short of a miracle’ – Rescuers Find Boy with Autism Missing for 3 Days
item.description: A six-year-old boy with autism, missing for three days in Kentucky, was found safe by volunteer searchers. How you can help: Ask your local search and rescue team about volunteering; most train new members. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm acquired by conservation group planning to open it to public
item.description: A conservation group bought Jimmy Carter's family farm to protect it and open it to the public. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers who saw a doorbell video raised 76,000 dollars for a woman who works full time as a caregiver. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World’s Driest Desert Erupts into Record-Breaking Bloom Boom (LOOK)
item.description: Chile's Atacama Desert has burst into a record bloom, with about 200 plant species in flower. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
item.description: A 450-million-year-old relative of starfish was found with its soft tissue preserved. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Actor, 85, takes to the stage despite Alzheimer’s diagnosis
item.description: An 85-year-old actor keeps performing on stage after an Alzheimer's diagnosis. Source: Positive News.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four volunteers finished more than a year in Nasa's simulated Mars habitat, growing food and rationing supplies. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
item.description: After a 40-year search, CERN found evidence of a particle decay that happens once in 10 billion. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric hydrofoil ferries, which rise above the water and use far less energy, are starting US service. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
item.description: Researchers traced a gut-to-brain pathway that explains how people come to enjoy bitter tastes like coffee. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Man’s Halloween Skeletons Prove Perfect Treat to Woman Battling Breast Cancer
item.description: A man's front-yard skeleton display became a weekly lift for a woman driving to cancer treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding play corners, childcare help and flexible advising so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Interpreting Autistic Cues Is Difficult, a Teen Built an App That’s Helping Hundreds of Families
item.description: A teenager taught himself machine learning and built an app that helps 700 families read autistic children's cues. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Glowworms Shine Again in the UK from Larvae Reared Pro Bono in Garden Shed
item.description: Glowworms are shining again at UK sites, from larvae a volunteer rears in his garden shed. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Leave a corner of your garden unlit and unmown; glowworms need dark, rough grass. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A UCLA study suggests a natural molecule may ease brain fog and fatigue after breast cancer treatment. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
item.description: Nasa set out a plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with an orbital test in 2027. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
item.description: Stickier ocean particles carry up to six times more carbon to the deep sea, improving climate models. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: A fossil site in Colombia preserves a rich ancient sea of giant reptiles and sharks. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dogs Can Sniff-Out Invasive Plant Species With High Accuracy to Curb Their Destruction
item.description: Volunteer dogs in Germany learned to sniff out invasive plants with high accuracy, so they can be removed early. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Choose native plants for your garden and never tip garden waste in the wild. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Lucky Bird Found in Storm Drain a Mile From Home After Passing Driver Happens to Spot it Hopping in
item.description: A pet budgie blown out of a window in a storm was spotted in a drain a mile away and returned home. How you can help: If you find a lost pet, post in local community groups; most reunions start there. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Baby Saved After Racing Heartbeat Detected by Family Doberman
item.description: A family dog's persistent crying led parents to find their baby's racing heartbeat in time for treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Adventurer Finally Hugs Mom After 28-Year Walk Around the World From Home in UK
item.description: After 28 years and 31,000 miles walking around the world, a man reached home in Hull and hugged his mother. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
item.description: Evidence shows ancient Europe was open woodland and meadow with grazing animals, a guide for rewilding. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: People Around the World Help Buy Royal Estate for Wildlife Conservation
item.description: Donors around the world raised millions to buy an estate where curlews, lapwings and rare bumblebees live. How you can help: Give to a land trust buying habitat in your region; small gifts add up to whole estates. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Spends 12 Days Returning Lost Cash a Laborer Needed for His Daughter
item.description: A man in Brazil spent 12 days tracing the owner of lost cash, a labourer saving for his daughter. How you can help: Hand found cash or valuables to the police or a nearby business so the owner can trace them. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Spark: When Communities Own the Land, Housing Stays Affordable
item.description: Community land trusts are keeping homes affordable by holding the land in shared ownership. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Find out whether a community land trust works in your area; many welcome new members. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: What went right this week: the good news that matters
item.description: A weekly roundup: nature restored at record scale, and Barbados ended HIV transmission to babies. Source: Positive News.

item.title: The butterfly effect: a brighter way to make paint?
item.description: Researchers are copying butterfly wing structures to make coloured coatings without chemical pigments. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: A Montana guest ranch employs autistic adults as wranglers, guides, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Personalized brain therapy hits 68 percent remission for PTSD
item.description: A personalised brain stimulation therapy cleared by the FDA brought PTSD remission in 68% of trial patients. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Who needs a golden ticket? The race to future-proof chocolate
item.description: A student made chocolate from cocoa grown in England, testing varieties suited to a changing climate. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: What if we stop treating social care like a service? This village shows the way
item.description: An English village runs social care as a shared community, with residents looking after one another. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Check in on an older neighbour this week; shared care starts with small regular visits. Source: Positive News.

item.title: What went right this week: renewed hope for the Brazilian Amazon, plus more
item.description: A weekly roundup: new hope for the Brazilian Amazon, and a skin cancer vaccine showing promise. Source: Positive News.

item.title: The Student Exchange Program That Never Leaves the U.S.
item.description: A US exchange programme sends students to live in very different communities within their own country. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Smartphones, ancient tracking skills and a future for desert lions
item.description: Namibian rangers pair live tracking data with old tracking skills, and desert lions are recovering. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Positive News.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community and purpose through small-scale farming. How you can help: Buy from a small farm near you, or join a community growing project. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants to safety so its Victorian Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer
item.description: A fossil kept in a drawer since 1985 turns out to be the first dinosaur bone found in Antarctica. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
